author: greystroke
content: Have thevlean ethereum researchers expressed any opinions about what slot times they feel comfortable they'll be able to prove on consumer gpus in the next 2-3 years? It would be helpful to have rough sense of how aggressive we can be with shortening slot times without delaying the transition to zkproofs.

author: tersec
content: zk proofs are currently taking $50k (optimistically) or $100k USD hardware. none of this is realistically "consumer'

author: tersec
content: it's a centralization thing, one is ok with it or not, but nothing to do with "consumer"

author: greystroke
content: I think the logic is more that it is consumer available hardware and not confined to hard to procure ASICs requiring data center power infrastructure.  Besides, there are plenty of enthusiast whales who will drop $100k on gpus, especially if it profitable. Plenty of old school Ethereum miners did that from their garage/basement/shack.

author: tersec
content: ok, sure, different definition of "consumer", I guess. anyone can put together enough 5090s

author: greystroke
content: I feel like the ship has sailed on zkproving on consumer gpus that could,  at least in theory, be run on-prem with 8-16 GPUs, being the way forward. But do we have any idea how much this should constrain shorter slot times? I've heard <@486501030046203915> mention 10s as slot time that some lean teams may be supportive of as a start.
